notes: The current offline seed contains 513 records: 79 sources, 16 products, 5 published catalogue offers, 3 FX observations and 410 benchmarks.

The September 2026 CSO wage source adds 90 governorate/category base-wage observations normalized by an explicit 8-hour day. Six added Iraqi fabrication/supply sources are capability leads only; they add no offers or supplier matches.

The v10 frame review evaluates all 3,183 requirements and has zero compatible priced matches. The v10 balanced federation review evaluates 137 of 7,042 requirements, with 6,905 pending, zero compatible priced matches and nine unsent RFQ drafts.

The v9 procurement BOM preserves 31,989 physical scopes, 2,269 manufacturing groups and 27,216 located occurrences, with 4,773 unlocated obligations separate. Its 191 packages and eight demand lines are not complete purchase assemblies; commercial order quantities remain unknown.

The 20% domestic estimate allowance applies only to source-priced material plus assumed direct base-wage hours. It is unallocated and does not establish overhead, profit, tax, contingency, quality, tooling, transport or installation.

The September concrete recipe is a statistical material-plus-labour scenario. Its same-candidate mapped totals preserve 81 groups and 486 occurrences for each location/hour case; the mix and shop hours are not qualified.

GFRP scenarios use UK catalogue-listed cloth/resin inputs converted at a dated non-executable CBI rate plus assumed Iraqi base-wage labour. Core, adhesive, tooling, employer burden and fabrication cost remain open; these are not locally produced laminate costs.

No supplier communication was sent. No supplier offer, compatible priced railway group, complete installed cost, physical qualification or release state is established; the selected reference remains unchanged.

limitations: The 2025 CSO regional bulletin contributes Iraqi-origin construction-material and governorate/category wage benchmarks. Source-table zeros remain unavailable; three concrete recipes are held where at least one input price is missing.

Regional 2025 and 2026 Baghdad estimates use explicit material + assumed labour hours + 20% scenarios. Only the 2025 Baghdad concrete scenario is mapped to exact research-candidate nominal concrete groups and original occurrences. Neither is a finished beam or installed civil cost.

New factory and procurement leads are not operational-capacity evidence, technically accepted products or supplier quotations. Import report, price-image and construction-bulletin leads add no parsed price observations.

The 2024 CSO report is a modeled private-building estimate that uses 2024 permits and price/wage bulletins with material-use ratios from a 2012 survey; its cost/quantity ratios are historical statistical indicators, not observed supplier transactions.
The 2024 report excludes Kurdistan Region; the 2025 wage comparator uses the Baghdad governorate annual construction-worker average.
Normal grit is not confirmed to be interchangeable with the 2025 CSO crushed-gravel category; grading, strength and delivery scope are unknown.
The concrete recipe and labour hours are sensitivity assumptions, not a mix design, verified yield, timed factory route or candidate-specific bill of quantities.
The 20% uplift applies only to declared material plus direct labour and is an unallocated planning allowance, not verified overhead, profit, tax or contingency.
